section_summary: This section records the sale of securities through Japanese liquidation agencies, including detailed share-sale tables and a statement of securities still held in March 1948. A State Department memorandum questions the slow pace of sales and whether the shares might become concentrated among newly wealthy buyers. Later correspondence concerns a Swiss-held Japanese bond, a proposed cotton credit, and public questions about United States aid to Japan. The section ends with a securities-sale chart that continues beyond page 624.

subfiles.title: Share offerings to employees and local residents
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: A continuing table lists shares offered to employees and local residents.
subfiles.summary: Final table entries record offerings in Tokyo, Kyoto and Takasaki.

subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 2: List of stocks disposed of up to February 21, 1948
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: The enclosure tabulates shares sold by securities liquidation agencies and the methods used.
subfiles.summary: Summary tables give shares, face values and proceeds for sales by S.C.L.C., C.I.L.C. and H.C.L.C. Detailed lists identify issues sold in 1947 and early 1948, with offering dates, buyers, shares sold and proceeds. The enclosure also lists C.I.L.C. sales before S.C.L.C. was established and H.C.L.C. sales before and after its establishment.

subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 3: Securities held by constituent agencies
subfiles.from: Office of the Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: A table reports securities still held by liquidation agencies as of March 20, 1948.
subfiles.summary: Lists agency holdings by security type.

subfiles.title: Swiss Legation memorandum transmitting a bond declaration
subfiles.about: The Legation forwards an additional Swiss bank declaration concerning Japanese bonds.
subfiles.summary: Requests transmission of a February 13 declaration from Banque Cantonale de Zurich.

subfiles.title: Banque Cantonale de Zurich declaration of Oriental Development bonds
subfiles.to: Swiss Bankers Association, Service des Dépôts
subfiles.about: The bank reports Japanese dollar bonds owned by a Swiss national and held in New York.
subfiles.summary: Reports $25,000 in Oriental Development bonds held at Chase National Bank and explains the late declaration.

subfiles.title: Proposed Japanese cotton credit
subfiles.about: Draper reports terms negotiated with commercial banks for a Japanese cotton credit.
subfiles.summary: Describes a 3 percent interest rate, a possible reduction if a gold fund reaches the United States, and a capped contingency for bank expenses.

subfiles.title: Illegible routing form
subfiles.about: A largely illegible standard form appears between the cotton-credit letter and the following memorandum.
subfiles.summary: Routing details cannot be read reliably.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on the sale of securities through liquidation agencies
subfiles.about: Green assesses a despatch on slow securities sales and the risk of concentrated ownership.
subfiles.summary: Green reports that roughly 4 percent of liquidated shares had been resold by March 1948 and that no bonds or debentures had been sold. He considers Bane's concern that wealthy postwar buyers could acquire the shares, while noting Welch's expectation of faster sales and legal restraints on excessive concentration.

subfiles.title: Senate referral of constituent's letter
subfiles.about: The Senate requests a reply about aid to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Refers the attached constituent letter for a response.

subfiles.title: Mrs. Jedd King's letter to Senator Vandenberg
subfiles.about: King asks why the United States is giving money to Japan and raises other foreign-policy objections.
subfiles.summary: Questions aid to Japan, favors a repayable textile loan, and comments on China, military training and immigration.

subfiles.title: State Department reply to Senator Vandenberg
subfiles.from: Charles E. Bohlen, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The Department supplies language answering Mrs. King's question about aid to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Explains occupation expenditures as necessary to prevent disease and unrest and support democratization. It also argues that raw materials such as cotton could revive Japanese exports and eventually reduce reliance on United States aid.

subfiles.title: Securities sold by Closed Institutions Liquidation Commission, May 1946–July 1947
subfiles.about: A continuing chart lists securities offered and sold from May 28, 1946, through July 1, 1947.
subfiles.summary: The chart records individual share issues, offering dates and methods, numbers of buyers, shares sold or unsold, and sale proceeds. Its columns alternate across facing pages. The chart continues beyond page 624.
